A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Di-Fusion work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A-I are readable and can be reliably matched despite layout changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original denoising experiments on real MRI data and simulated fastMRI data, downstream clinical-task evaluations, and ablations in Section 4 and Appendices E-I.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experimental results, including simulation metrics in Table 1 and downstream-task and ablation results in the appendices.

M1.justification: Section 3, Algorithms 1-2, and Appendix B retain the same Fusion interpolation, Di noise construction, latter-step training objective, Run-Walk sampling, and adaptive termination.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Stanford HARDI, Sherbrooke 3-Shell, PPMI, and five fastMRI noise simulations. Denoising, tractography, microstructure fitting, and diffusion-signal estimation coverage is unchanged.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged across the real-data, simulation, and appendix experiments, including the Patch2Self variants and Neighbor2Neighbor comparisons. Newly cited Corruption2Self is not added to the evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Training budgets, model configurations, three-fold microstructure evaluation, preprocessing, metrics, and simulation procedures remain unchanged in Section 4 and Appendix D. The appendix sensitivity experiments also retain their settings.

E4.justification: Both retain the same component ablations, sampling and termination tests, mixed-b-value and reduced-volume studies, Patch2Self sensitivity comparisons, and DDM2 first-stage analysis. Relocated appendix material does not add analyses.

E5.justification: Both specify three simulation runs for Nr2N, DDM2, and Di-Fusion, report means and standard deviations in Table 1, and retain the SNR/CNR distribution summaries in Figure S12. No uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: Table 1, Tables S2-S7, and the qualitative findings retain their results. For example, Di-Fusion's Simulation 1 PSNR remains 19.91 dB and SSIM remains 39.05%; its CSD-CC R2 in Table S2 remains 0.967.

T1.justification: The mathematical construction and Appendices B-C derivations of diffusion trajectories, noise variance, and sampling speed are unchanged. The new noise-scope paragraph provides an applicability qualification without revising the formal arguments.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: single-stage self-supervised denoising, stable latter-step training, adaptive refinement, and claimed state-of-the-art downstream performance.

C2.justification: Section 5 expands v1's inference-time and hallucination limitations with a specific noise-scope caveat. v3 states a thermal-noise focus modeled as additive Gaussian processes, excludes physiological artifacts such as cardiac pulsation, and acknowledges possible difficulty with signal-dependent noise.

D1.justification: The abstract replaces the statement that code is in supplementary material with a direct pointer to the FouierL/Di-Fusion GitHub repository. This changes the documented access route; Appendix D's implementation details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds Corruption2Self (Tu et al., 2025), DiffusionBlend (Song et al., 2024), and six references supporting the new noise/artifact discussion. The central positioning against Patch2Self and DDM2 remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 updates affiliations, contact information, and corresponding-author identification, adds acknowledgments, and makes localized additions to related work and limitations. The overall section structure and scientific narrative are retained.

P2.justification: The expanded front matter and text cause layout and appendix-float reflow. For example, Figure S32 moves from sharing a page with Appendix I to a separate page after its discussion. Figure content and table structures remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v3 makes applicability more explicit by distinguishing thermal-noise denoising from physiological-artifact correction and acknowledging signal-dependent noise limitations. Added related work and a direct code-repository pointer also improve documentation. These are limited gains; the method and supporting empirical and mathematical evidence remain unchanged.
